 (WJAR) — Lindsay Clancy will be back in court on Monday, as a judge is expected to set a date for the retrial.
 The Duxbury, Massachusetts, woman is accused of strangling her three young children.
 The case has put a spotlight on postpartum psychosis.
 The first trial ended in a hung jury.
 View post on X 
 Judge William Sullivan, who also oversaw the first murder trial, denied her team's request to dismiss the three murder indictments against her.
 He also denied a motion to question the holdout juror from that first trial.
 MORE: Judge denies motion to dismiss charges against Lindsay Clancy 
 The prosecution also received a loss. Judge Sullivan rejected its bid to prevent lawyers from discussing the case with the media.
 During a hearing two weeks ago, defense lawyer Kevin Reddington still had a lot of questions for the judge. The prosecution has not said if it will retry Clancy for first-degree murder or a lesser charger.
 The hearing will be livestreamed on turnto10.com , the NBC 10 Facebook page , and the NBC 10 WJAR YouTube channel .
